project_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company

project_metadata.job_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company
project_metadata.job_description:
** Thank you for sending your proposals. We look forward to reviewing them all soon. Please bear with us though as we are a bit busy but we will get back to you as soon as possible!**

We are looking for an experienced logo designer to create an original logo for our UK-based street food business, Global Dough.

Global Dough serves globally inspired street food built around dough and flatbreads, including pizzas, naan breads, wraps and other freshly prepared street food cooked in wood-fired and tandoor ovens.

What we need:
A clean, unique and professional logo
Minimalist
Modern-retro styling (not cartoonish)
Strong enough to work on the side of a food truck (see attached pic)
Simple, bold and highly legible from a distance
Suitable for social media, our website (not produced yet), menus, signage, clothing and packaging
Typography-led design preferred
We are open to subtle graphic elements, but do not want obvious globes, chef hats, food clipart or generic AI-style icons
We only want one example of a logo with subtle graphic elements. The other concepts need to be just typography as that's our preference.

Colours:
Burnt orange
Black
White

Logo should have the name of the company and our strapline:
Global Dough
Seriously Tasty Street Food

Deliverables:
3–5 initial concepts
Up to 3 revision rounds
Full colour version
Black version
White version
Vector files (AI, EPS, SVG)
PNG files with transparent background
JPGS
Font details supplied

Copyright & Ownership:
The final logo must be completely original.

No stock logos, copyrighted elements, template-based logos, or AI-generated logo artwork.

When applying please provide:

Examples of food hospitality logos you have designed.
Confirmation that your work is original and suitable for trademark use.
Your estimated turnaround time.
Your fixed-price quote.
Upon final payment, all intellectual property rights must transfer exclusively to us. The logo should be suitable for future trademark registration.

Budget: £150–£200

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please give me a moment to check the files, Tessa, and I’ll resend them shortly. I’m sorry about the issue, and thank you for your patience and for bringing it to my attention.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Before we proceed, could you confirm whether the fixed cost covers the brand colours and fonts that will be set out for us? The truck’s illuminated lettering reads ‘Copper Crust Truck’ and uses Clab, but we do not necessarily want or need that same typeface for the logo. We hope to hire you; we simply wanted to clarify which colour and font guidelines would be produced first.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Everything required for a consistent brand identity going forward will be covered: the fixed cost includes both the brand colors and the font.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’m available to begin immediately. Could you let me know whether you have a particular completion timeline in mind for the project?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: With both of us busy with our day-to-day work while trying to launch this start-up, there is no immediate rush. Would completion within the next 5 weeks work for you? We still need to complete your hire contract before proceeding, so please bear with us.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That timing is perfect for me. I’m now looking forward to receiving the contract.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I appreciate the offer and will return with the initial concepts.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Before any concept work begins, we’ll send over some examples we like, although we’re also interested in your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: When you’re ready, please send across any concepts or references you like. I’ll review them carefully before beginning the creative process, then combine your inspirations with my own ideas to develop something unique and memorable for your brand. That sounds like a great approach, and I’m looking forward to seeing what inspires you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’m looking forward to receiving the inspiration concepts, Tessa.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: It’s been one of those weeks, so please bear with us! We haven’t forgotten.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’ll be ready when it arrives.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Attached is an AI-generated draft logo that we made while simply experimenting with chat gpt. It is only inspiration: we still want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted the proposal. We do, however, like its colours because they fit the look and feel of the Copper Crust truck.

The company is called ‘Copper Crust’, so the logo must not contain the word ‘truck’. The mobile catering truck is only one part of the wider business. Copper Crust will operate that truck, sell food online and may also supply other caterers or kitchens. That broader scope is why the company name excludes ‘truck’, while the existing strapline remains unchanged. Would you be happy to discuss any of this before accepting the offer?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: As explained above, the truck shown here represents only one part of the wider business.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To reflect your vision, I’ll develop several concepts and add a creative touch so that each design feels visually appealing and unique.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: My usual approach is to share the initial drafts before accepting the offer. That lets clients review the proposed direction first and feel completely comfortable before moving forward.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Whichever timing makes you most comfortable will work for me. I can present the initial concepts and accept the offer afterward, or I can accept it immediately if that is what you would prefer.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Let’s use your suggested approach and review the initial drafts before the offer is accepted. Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The initial drafts are ready for you to review, Tessa, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. Please tell me about any revisions, refinements, iterations or other changes you would like; I’m happy to keep working with you until the result fully matches your vision.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: After looking through the drafts, Julian (my spouse, who leads the kitchen and founded the venture!!) and I added our consolidated feedback to the attached powerpoint. Thank you so much for the concepts. Hopefully our comments make sense, but please ask if anything is unclear. All best, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thanks for sending the feedback, Tessa. I’ll review your comments and return with the updated designs.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The designs are ready for review, Tessa; please take a look and share your feedback.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
The graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline both work well for us. Of the concepts, we like the 2nd and 6th one; the typeface in the 5th one feels too plain. Our concern with the flame in the 6th one is that someone unfamiliar with our name may not recognise it as an ‘O’, although we do like the treatment.

Could you test every suggested solution: enclosing the flame within an ‘O’, shaping the flame more clearly like an ‘O’, and superimposing it onto an ‘O’?

For logo 6, please also show us how a slightly larger ‘dough’ would look. The strapline could stand out either by outlining every letter with a thin black pencil line or by slightly brightening the orange tones in its lettering. We like the character of the font used for copper crust, particularly the G. We wondered whether a couple of the other letters could gain a little character too, but it would be better to handle revisions one stage at a time because the current font may already be suitable. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’ll go through the feedback carefully and will come back to you if anything needs clarification. Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Your feedback has now been incorporated, Tessa. Please review the updated designs and share your thoughts.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Work has completely swamped us, but thank you for sending these. We’ll get back to you over the weekend.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sure, take your time!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Apologies for the delay. Julian prefers number 7, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I would still like the ‘copper crust’ font to have a little more character, reflecting food that will be truly authentic, freshly cooked and full of flavours from around the world. The interesting G shape in both words appeals to me. Could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without overdoing it? Thanks, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’ll explore what can be done with those letterforms, Tessa, and return with an updated draft. Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Without reducing the logo’s quality or readability, these two options represent about as much character as the letterforms can support. Any further treatment would weaken the clean, refined appearance and make the logo less versatile across different applications.

The changes therefore add subtle personality while retaining the brand’s premium, authentic feel. In my view, that gives the logo a distinctive touch without sacrificing its balance or professionalism.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: When you’ve reviewed the revised options, please share your thoughts with me.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you for these—we’re nearly there!
1\. For the fifth logo, please reduce the U and H so they match the height of the remaining letters in ‘DOUGH’.
2\. At the top-right of the H in DOUGH, please flip the feature so that it mirrors the top of the U in DOUGH.
3\. Finally, please give the top of the D in DOUGH the same feature used at the top of the B in GLOBAL.

The attached annotated screenshot shows what we mean. Once those revisions are complete, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain a ‘clean’ appearance while gaining the character. Many thanks, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Absolutely, Tessa. I’ll implement those changes and return with an updated design.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please review.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I mistakenly thought I had already replied! We’d like to proceed with the final version shown above, rev8-11. Thank you.

Am I right that the logo will be provided both with and without the black box, since that background will not suit every use? Will we also receive every colour variant you have shown?

For the main logo, our preference is the top-row treatment from the final version: graduated orange for ‘global’, black for ‘dough’ and graduated orange for the strapline.

We now need the logo guidelines and every relevant file type for online use, social media, the truck and hard-copy materials such as pull-up banners, printed menus and uniforms. Given the large file sizes, how will you share them—through Wetransfer? Thank you, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
To continue with the remaining work, could you approve the first milestone and activate the second when you have a moment, Tessa?

The logo will be supplied both with and without the black box. For the colour variants, are you requesting every version explored during the design process, or only the standard full-color, black and white versions?

All necessary formats will be delivered, including fully editable source files suitable for print, web, social media, signage, merchandise and other applications. The final package will also contain the font details and color codes used in the approved design.

One point to clarify is that logo guidelines were not part of the original project scope and are normally handled as a separate project. There are two options:

Basic Logo Usage Guidelines – $280
This covers logo variations, clear space, minimum size, color palette, typography, and basic do’s and don’ts.

Complete Brand Guidelines – $425
This includes everything in the basic guide, plus a fuller brand system covering typography hierarchy, imagery style, iconography, layout principles, brand applications, stationery and t-shirt mockups, and detailed usage rules.

I’d be happy to produce either version so that the logo can be applied consistently and professionally across future branding materials.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Could you confirm whether the first $240 has been received and whether the second $240 has been released? I’m unsure whether I completed everything required to release the latter amount, so I’ll check again.

Perhaps “guidelines” was not the right term. Earlier, you confirmed that the fixed cost included the brand colors and font, providing what we need to maintain a consistent brand identity. Those details are what I meant rather than a separate guidelines project.

For the colour versions, we only need the three you stated above. Thanks, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Payment for the first milestone has been released. The second milestone must first be activated and funded before its payment can be released.

As discussed, the final files will include the brand colors and fonts at no additional cost. I’ll include the requested color versions as well.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Has the final payment been released now?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The milestone is now activated, and you can release its payment after I submit the final files. I expect to deliver those files within an hour.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Although I won’t be able to review all the deliverables until tomorrow evening, I’ve released the final payment in the meantime.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Please take as much time as you need to review everything. After you are completely satisfied with the final deliverables, I’d really appreciate you closing the contract. I am expecting a 5-star rating along with some positive feedback, which would mean a great deal and help my profile.

Thank you again. If any final adjustments are needed, I’ll be happy to assist.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I’ve only now had a chance to sit down with my laptop and open the delivered files. The colour codes document gives an error, so I’m unable to open it. The jpgs and pdfs work without any problem, but I cannot open the AI, EPS or PSD files. Among the png files, only logo 7 opens correctly; all the others fail to open properly.

I also need to know whether you used an existing font for the logo or created the lettering yourself. If it was custom-made, which font should we use on the website and other materials to complement or match the logo, for example in some headers? Thanks, Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Tessa,

I appreciate you checking the files and telling me about the problems.

Only Adobe Photoshop can open the PSD file. The AI and EPS files, meanwhile, need Adobe Illustrator or another compatible vector-editing program. Without those applications installed, the files will not open correctly.

I’ll investigate the PNG files that aren’t opening properly and send corrected versions.

Because the logo lettering is completely custom-made, it is not based on any specific font. I can, however, recommend a very similar font that complements the logo and works well across your website, headings, and other branding materials to maintain a consistent look.

If you’d like suggestions, please let me know and I can provide a few font options.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thanks for clarifying things. The colour codes document still won’t open for me, so I’ll wait to hear back about the PNG files. If screenshots of what appears when I try opening them would help, I can send those later. And yes, please recommend fonts that would complement the logo.

Thanks,
Tessa

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Tessa,

I’ll start by resending the colour codes document and investigating the PNG files. If I still can’t identify the issue, I’ll ask you to provide screenshots later.

I’ll also prepare a few font recommendations that complement the logo and send them over shortly. No worries, and thanks for letting me know!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thank you. To tick all those boxes and allow us to trademark the logo in due course, could you also confirm in writing that we own the copyright?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
You’re very welcome! To confirm that the copyright has been assigned to you, I can prepare a Copyright Transfer Certificate that you can retain for your records and use when applying for a trademark.

Preparing the certificate carries an additional charge of $120. Would you like me to proceed? Once you confirm, I’ll get it ready for you.

messages.text: Before proceeding, could you email me a draft or template certificate so I can check whether the wording is sufficient?

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To personalize the trademark certificate, please provide the full legal name and address you want included. I can’t complete it until I have those details.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:

You can see the text and artwork clearly if you zoom in. As another check, drag and drop each PNG file into any web browser or paint app; it should display properly there without issues.

Please try that and let me know what you see.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:

Fonts Name:

Haboro Soft Normal Extra Bold

messages.text: When I can, yes, I’ll review it.

messages.text: For the certificate, could you also create a separate milestone and activate it, please?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi, the certificate is included here.

Could you please close the contract as well? I’m expecting a 5-star rating along with a positive review.

Working with you was a pleasure. Thank you, and I hope we’ll have another opportunity to collaborate in the future!
